summary: Preserved PR 2952's NCCL RMA implementation and compatibility fixes, reproduced PR 3021's remaining window-accessor scoping defect against exact candidate commit 34d861306b4fdce616d2260d9d9f52655d6ef145, and corrected it by publishing both native accessor bindings to the module globals consumed by _collect_windows_for_comm(). Added a loader-level regression proving a non-null handle is surfaced.

tests.what_was_measured: Candidate baseline: 18 passed and 2 two-GPU tests skipped; confirms the reviewed defect was not covered by the candidate suite.
Rebuilt and loaded nccl_allocator.so with -lrccl; both native accessor symbols existed, but both Python module globals were None and collection returned [].
19 passed and 2 hardware tests skipped; new regression drives the allocator loader and verifies synthetic native handle 0xA11CE is returned by _collect_windows_for_comm().
The real rebuilt allocator exports both symbols and both module globals now hold ctypes function pointers. The arbitrary unregistered communicator correctly returns no windows.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) was visible under torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2. The loader touched the ROCm device and created a memory pool, but no GPU numerical RMA operation was executed; the required two-rank NVIDIA NCCL/NVLink topology was unavailable.

remaining_limitations: The real two-rank NVIDIA NCCL 2.30/NVLink ring put_signal/wait_signal handshake remains unverified because the assigned environment has one AMD GPU.
The successful gfx950 RCCL allocator rebuild validates compilation, loading, and exported accessor symbols, but does not qualify NVIDIA NCCL RMA behavior.
No registered non-NULL RCCL/NCCL window could be produced on this single-rank topology; non-NULL handle propagation is covered deterministically by the loader regression.
